evidence: Source: app/main.py:28 reads the user value `key = request.args.get("status", "open")`. But app/main.py:29 maps it through `REPORT_STATUSES.get(key, "OPEN")`, a fixed dict defined at app/main.py:8-12. So `status` can only be one of the constants "OPEN", "SHIPPED", "REFUNDED". Unknown keys fall back to "OPEN". The f-string at app/main.py:31 never receives attacker-controlled text, and none of the constants contain quotes or SQL syntax. Side note: the route (app/main.py:25) has no auth check, although its docstring says it is for the operations dashboard. That exposes aggregate order counts but is not SQL injection.
recommended_fix: No security fix needed for injection. As hardening, switch to a bound parameter (`WHERE status = ?`, `(status,)`) so the code stays safe if the allowlist is ever removed, and the scanner stops flagging it. Separately, check whether /reports/status should require authentication.
title: False positive: /reports/status interpolates only allowlisted constants
